atoms.b: Authors use their words to create a theme for a poem. A theme can be a picture you see in your mind while reading the poem or a feeling or mood you get from the words.

atoms.b:
Once there was an elephant,
Who tried to use the ((telephant)).
No! No! I mean an ((elephone)),
Who tried to use the telephone-
(Dear me! I am not certain quite
That even now I’ve got it right.)

Howe'er it was, he got his trunk
Entangled in the ((telephunk));
The more he tried to get it free,
The louder buzzed the ((telephee))-
(I fear I’d better drop the song
Of ((elephop)) and (( telephong))!)

end.text: The narrator mixes the words elephant and telephone together. The mix-ups are funny and also add to the theme of confusion.
